top_signals.title: North Korea’s Irregular Warfare After Ukraine
top_signals.summary:
Pyongyang has a long history of conducting irregular warfare and asymmetric operations: Look no further than the 1968 Blue House raid or the 1996 submarine incursion as the most pressing examples. More often than not, North Korea failed to achieve the intended objectives of its missions and lost its commandos. Despite failures, the regime pressed on, and now, over thirty years after the sub incursion, it has the combat experience of its special operations forces in Kursk to leverage. top_signals.title: Stocks Rise as Bonds Halt Selloff on Oil Cooldown: Markets Wrap
top_signals.summary: The final stretch of a jittery week on Wall Street saw a rebound in stocks as oil prices fell, halting a selloff in bonds that had roiled financial markets around the world.

top_signals.title: Yen Rises as Japanese Officials Say Weak Currency is a Problem
top_signals.summary: The yen was headed for its best day in almost three weeks, lifted as Japanese officials discussed the problems of a weak currency in meeting with their US counterparts.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: Argentina’s 10% Yields Tempt Bond Buyers as Election Risks Build
top_signals.summary: Argentine bonds at double-digit yields are proving attractive to investors willing to shrug off fears about President Javier Milei’s sinking popularity ahead of elections late next year.
